title: Passive-region warmup validation and circuit-breaker probing
creator: Anika Rao
description: Objective: Create and validate a deterministic warmup and probe regimen for passive regions to ensure fast activation with bounded risk. We will automate traffic-probing and circuit-breaker exercise sequences, verify backup/restore integrity, and exercise load-shedding rules under controlled conditions. Focus is on measurable SLO impact, observable rollback criteria, and a reproducible runbook.
acceptance_criteria: Automated warmup job completes in <15m for passive region with KV cache prefetch hit >= 85%
Circuit-breaker probing sequence triggers expected failure modes without causing primary-region degradation
Backup restoration test to staging completes with data integrity check (checksums) and no orphaned tokens
Load-shedding policy reduces offered load to target rate limit while preserving control-plane availability
Runbook steps validateable via dashboards and an after-action report summarizing SLO delta and remediation tasks
runbook_checklist: 1) Schedule maintenance window and notify on-call, support, and product
2) Snapshot tokenstore and config state; archive to S3 (retain for 30 days)
3) Run warmup job in passive region using recent workload traces
4) Execute circuit-breaker probe suite (gradual error injection + latency spikes)
5) Apply controlled load-shedding profile (simulate 50-70% traffic drop)
6) Trigger backup restore to staging cluster and run checksum + smoke tests
7) Monitor SLO dashboards (p95 latency, error-rate) and cost metrics
8) If any threshold breached, initiate abort flow and failback steps
9) Collect logs, traces, and KV cache metrics for post-mortem
10) Publish after-action report and update runbook
test_plan: Warmup: replay 2 hours of production trace at 1x to passive region; validate cache warming and cold-start latency
CB Probes: inject HTTP 500s to 5% of requests for 2m, then increase to 20% for 1m; validate CB trips and auto-recovery
Load-shed: ramp client traffic to 120% of baseline with shedding rules active; assert control-plane keepalive and token issuance remain within limits
Backup/Restore: snapshot, delete, restore dataset subset (5%), verify checksums and token integrity
Rollback: confirm traffic re-routing back to primary within 3m and KV store reconciliation within 30m
observability_and_metrics: Dashboards: kube-rrt, runtime-p95, tokenstore-checksums, cb-trip-count, shedding-rate
Key metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, 5xx rate, circuit-breaker open duration, cache hit %, restore validation pass/fail
Alerting: SLO-Delta >5% sustained for 5m, CB stuck-open >10m, restore-failure
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Warmup job overwhelms destination GPUs -> Mitigation: limit concurrency and apply rate-limiter
Risk: Circuit-breaker probe leaks into primary -> Mitigation: strict routing isolation and header-based scoping
Risk: Restore reveals schema drift -> Mitigation: pre-restore schema validation and migration sandbox
Risk: Client-side retries amplify load during load-shedding -> Mitigation: deploy retry-budget enforcement and instruct SDK teams
implementation_notes: Warmup implementation will use batch replay service with KV prefetch hooks
Circuit-breaker probes implemented as traffic shadowing with injected faults and controlled latency via chaos-engine
Restore validation uses checksum tool (tools/restore-checksum v0.9) and token reconciliation scripts
Create a Canary job in CI to run lightweight probes on every runtime release (runtime-1.20 onwards)

after_action_template: Summary: one-paragraph incident-style summary of what we did and why
Impact: measured SLO delta, user-facing errors, and duration
Findings: list of root causes or unexpected observations
Action items: prioritized remediation with owners and due dates
Runbook updates: exact lines to change in the runbook and who will make the change
